title: USMNT’s Mauricio Pochettino expected to attend Atletico Madrid vs Tottenham
content:
Mauricio Pochettino is expected to attend Tuesday night’s Champions League first-leg tie between Atletico Madrid and Tottenham Hotspur.

The 54-year-old USMNT head coach will be an official guest of Atletico, and may have a watching brief over midfielder Johnny Cardoso, who is pushing to be included in Pochettino’s squad for this summer’s World Cup.

Cardoso has started in just 12 matches for Atletico this term and has featured in five of the club’s 10 Champions League games.

Pochettino and Spurs suffered heartbreak at the Madrid stadium in June 2019 when they were beaten 2-0 by Liverpool in the Champions League final. Five months later, the Argentine coach was sacked, bringing down the curtain on his five-and-a-half year spell in charge.

Tuesday’s last-16 first leg is Spurs’ first visit the ground since, and it will be Pochettino’s first time watching his former club from the stands — he twice beat Spurs while in charge of rivals Chelsea in the 2023-24 season — and will inevitably increase speculation about a possible return to north London in the summer.

Spurs will be looking to appoint a permanent head coach after placing Igor Tudor in charge until the end of the season, following the sacking of Thomas Frank last month.

Pochettino has made no secret of his interest in one day returning to the club and in December reiterated that he was “always thinking” about working in the Premier League again.

Tudor has lost his first three games in charge, leaving Spurs one point above the relegation zone with nine league games to play, and the Croatian admitted on Monday that the Champions League was not the club’s priority.

“We’re playing against a team who has a story in the Champions League, so they have experience and quality,” he said.

“We need to do our best in times that we need to grow. Also because our first aim is Premier League, this needs to be said publicly, it’s a normal thing. This is something extra, but that doesn’t mean we don’t want to go in the next round.”
